newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan names new Peru envoy on eve of Fujimori trip.
newsitem.headline: Japan names new Peru envoy on eve of Fujimori trip.

text.p: Japan appointed a veteran diplomat as its new ambassador to Peru on Tuesday as Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori was set to arrive on his first trip to Tokyo since the Lima hostage crisis ended in April.

Yoshizo Konishi, current ambassador to South Africa, was named to fill the post vacated when Morihisa Aoki was forced to resign in May to take responsibility for the four-month-old hostage standoff at his official residence in Lima.
The 63-year-old Konishi has experience in Latin America, having served as Tokyo's ambassador to Nicaragua.

Aoki, slammed by the Japanese media for lax security at the residence and for what some reports said was high-handed behavior, was reprimanded by the Foreign Ministry last month for his role in the hostage seizure.
Peru, however, gave Aoki it highest national honours for his grace and courage under pressure.
The hostage crisis ended on April 22 when Peruvian commandos stormed the residence to free the 72 hostages held since December 17 by rebels of the leftist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement.
A Peruvian hostage, two commandos and all 14 Peruvian captors died in the assault.
Fujimori is to arrive in Tokyo on Wednesday for a six-day visit that is to include talks with Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and tours of several regional cities.
